headline: South Asia: Pakistan, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia agree to rapid force deployment in the kingdom under Makkah pact
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: Pakistan, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia agree to rapid force deployment in the kingdom under Makkah pact.
- Asia: Saudi-Iran war risk grows as Riyadh resumes Yemen bombing.
- Western Russia: One dead and four injured in Russians attack on Kramatorsk – photos.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: Aboard the USS George Washington, young sailors adjust to war with Iran.
- Military Times, 23 hours ago: Aboard the USS George Washington, young sailors adjust to war with Iran.
Sailors must maintain a ​state of alert and readiness, heightened in the case of the George Washington due to the threat of Iranian attacks.
- Military Times, 23 hours ago: US Army tests counter-drone tech at Mexican border as cartel drone use rises.
The service is seeking to sharpen its defenses against the growing threat of drone use by cartels.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Doctors’ pay fight ends in major win.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 9 hours ago: Doctors’ pay fight ends in major win.
Following the Industrial Disputes Tribunal’s landmark ruling in favour of doctors in their long-running allowances dispute with the State, senior trade unionist Lambert Brown says the medical practitioners are ready to meet with the Government to implement the award. In a quick response on Monday, Brown said the doctors were pleased with the outcome. “We receive the award [ruling] just after 4 p.m. and we can confirm that award is in favour of the doctors and the two issues before the tribunal,” he said.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: One dead and four injured in Russians attack on Kramatorsk – photos.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 8 hours ago: One dead and four injured in Russians attack on Kramatorsk – photos.
Russian FPV drone strikes killed a woman and injured four others, including medical personnel, in targeted attacks on Kramatorsk on 5 October.
- The Moscow Times, 3 hours ago: Kremlin Warns Lithuania Lifting Nuclear Arms Ban Risks Escalation.
The move comes on the heels of Estonia announcing it was moving its troops closer to the country's border with Russia.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: More than 60% of Ukrainians willing to endure war as long as necessary – survey.
Despite intensified Russian reactive drone attacks, a KIIS survey reveals 62% of Ukrainians are prepared to continue resisting as long as needed
- Ukrainska Pravda, 4 hours ago: Russian drone drops explosives in Kherson Oblast, killing man.
A Russian drone dropped explosives near Kachkarivka in Kherson Oblast, killing a man; a woman was also killed in a separate attack the previous day.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Serbian Student Targeted by Spyware Attack Sues Authorities.
- Balkan Insight, 3 hours ago: Serbian Student Targeted by Spyware Attack Sues Authorities.
Lawyers for one of 14 people targeted by Pegasus spyware file criminal complaint against Serbian intelligence agency officials, police and the Israeli company behind the surveillance technology after institutions fail to react.
- Balkan Insight, 4 hours ago: Kosovo Protesters Against Hague Court Gather Again After Clashes.
After violent clashes on Monday night, protesters started to reassemble in Pristina to demand legal changes to curb the powers of the Kosovo Specialist Chambers war crimes court following convictions of guerrilla leaders.
- Politico Europe, 4 hours ago: Former German spy chief arrested for treason and espionage.
One of the greatest potential intelligence breaches in post-Cold War German history comes at a particularly sensitive time for the country’s scandal-plagued foreign intelligence agency.
- Politico Europe, 6 hours ago: Von der Leyen warns against EU budget cuts.
Commission president dismissed Germany's calls for big savings, arguing that they would undermine EU-wide priorities.

AFRICA
Persian Gulf Region - bottom line: Saudi Arabia says three wounded in attacks on airports near Yemen border.
- Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: Saudi Arabia says three wounded in attacks on airports near Yemen border.
Saudi aviation authority reports severe injuries and damage following Houthi strikes on Jazan and Najran airports.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Iranian women trained with missiles, drones as regime seeks recruits for ‘self-sacrifice’ campaign.
Iranian state media published images of women training in missile use, urban warfare, firearms, and drone operations as part of a new military training campaign.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Reflecting on three years of arts coverage since October 7: Balancing culture, tragedy - comment.
Over the past three years, as an arts and culture writer, I have tried my best to cope with the events of October 7 by striking a balance between arts chronicling those killed in the war.
- Jerusalem Post, just now: Opposing Israel's defense establishment, Katz threatens all-out war on Palestinian Authority.
Despite the defense minister's warning, IDF has insisted it has no intelligence pointing to an attack, and Shin Bet sources told the Post that they do not know of a concrete threat from the PA.
Africa - bottom line: Ethiopia: PM vows to secure sea access amid fears of return to war.
- Africanews, 17 hours ago: Ethiopia: PM vows to secure sea access amid fears of return to war.
Following almost two weeks of internal conflict that threatens a wider regional war in Ethiopia, the country's prime minister has vowed that government forces are ready to bring a rebel offensive under control.
- Africanews, 4 hours ago: Tigray violence drives risk of Ethiopia-Eritrea war, analyst says.
Renewed fighting between Ethiopian federal forces and Tigrayan rebels increases risks of an escalation into a wider regional conflict, according to International Crisis Group analyst Magnus Taylor.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 2 hours ago: Africa: Russia's Military Recruitment Networks Exploit Western Tech Platforms.
[ISS] African countries face an uphill battle in holding digital companies accountable for the use of their platforms in Russia's war effort.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 4 hours ago: Nigeria: NAF Releases Names of 25 Victims Killed in Military Plane Crash [full List].
[Vanguard] The Nigerian Air Force has released the names of 25 people killed in the aircraft crash that occurred in Igbokoda, Ondo State, on Monday.
South Africa: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Pakistan, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia agree to rapid force deployment in the kingdom under Makkah pact.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 19 hours ago: Pakistan, Turkiye, Saudi Arabia agree to rapid force deployment in the kingdom under Makkah pact.
Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye have agreed to deploy military forces and capabilities rapidly in the kingdom, the Foreign Office (FO) said on Monday following an emergency meeting of the Makkah Joint Defence Agreement in Riyadh. The three countries held an emergency meeting of the Strategic Political and Defence Committee (SPDC) of the Makkah Defence Alliance to address the security developments and threats facing Saudi Arabia, the FO statement said.
- The Hindu - International, 21 hours ago: Airstrikes, artillery hit north Ethiopia as government and rebels clash, sources say.
Air attacks killed at least 17 people northwest of Tigray’s capital Mekelle — which federal government forces took over the weekend — according to a bulletin circulated among humanitarian groups
- Dawn (Pakistan), 4 hours ago: 4 FBR officials, traffic policeman martyred in DI Khan attacks: police.
DERA ISMAIL KHAN: Four Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) officials were martyred in firing by unidentified assailants near Qureshi Mor in Dera Ismail Khan, while a separate attack on a highway traffic police mobile near the Mufti Mahmood Chowk bypass left a police official martyred and another injured, police said on Tuesday. Dera Ismail Khan District Police Officer Ziauddin Ahmad told Dawn that two of the four FBR officials were serving with the board on a contractual basis.
- The Hindu - International, 6 hours ago: Yemen, Saudi Arabia strike Houthis as counteroffensive gets underway.
The Yemeni military said it carried out more than 1,000 strikes and began an offensive against the Houthi-held capital, Sanaa, while the Saudi-led coalition supporting the internationally recognised government said 100 warplanes flew sorties at dawn
Asia - bottom line: Saudi-Iran war risk grows as Riyadh resumes Yemen bombing.
- South China Morning Post - China, 3 hours ago: Saudi-Iran war risk grows as Riyadh resumes Yemen bombing.
Iran and Saudi Arabia are edging dangerously closer to direct conflict, analysts warn, after Riyadh resumed major air strikes on Yemen’s Tehran-allied Houthi rebels this week, ending a four-year lull. More than 100 Saudi warplanes bombed rebel positions on Monday, enabling Yemeni government forces to retake much of the Red Sea coastal territory the Houthis seized last month. The Houthis had been aided by embedded Iranian military advisers. Analysts expect the Houthis to retaliate by intensifying...
- South China Morning Post - China, The Moscow Times, Al Jazeera - Middle East, one hour ago: Ukraine attacks Moscow region with 650 drones as both sides step up strikes.
A massive attack involving 650 drones targeted Moscow overnight, leaving at least two dead, Russian authorities said on Tuesday. Most of the drones were destroyed by air defences at long range, including 105 intercepted as they approached the capital, Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin wrote on Telegram. Russian state news agency Tass reported it was the second-largest drone attack on the capital region in the past two years. The dead included a 71-year-old man pulled from under the rubble ‌of a house...
- South China Morning Post - China, 5 hours ago: Why India is getting serious about ending the Ukraine war.
India’s recent push to become more involved in helping end the Russia-Ukraine war comes as the costs of the conflict continue to mount for New Delhi, amid the threat of US tariffs on major buyers of Russian energy and a recent drone attack on an Indian-owned pharmaceutical plant in Ukraine. Sunday morning’s drone attack destroyed a large part of Kusum Group’s factory in Sumy, killing one person and injuring several others. The company, which has manufactured generic medicines in Ukraine since...
- South China Morning Post - China, one hour ago: US firm to make battle-tested drones in Taiwan, boosting supply chain resilience.
Two combat-tested American drones could become part of Taiwan’s expanding unmanned arsenal as the island seeks to build a “drone shield” against the People’s Liberation Army. California-based defence technology company Aevex Aerospace is working with Taiwan’s Coretronic Intelligent Robotics Corporation (CIRC) to produce its Vandal and Onyx drones locally, combining lessons drawn from the war in Ukraine with the island’s electronics and manufacturing capabilities. Both aircraft have been tested...
Korean Peninsula - bottom line: North Korea turning to knock-off parts for missiles used in Ukraine: Report.
- NK News, 8 hours ago: North Korea turning to knock-off parts for missiles used in Ukraine: Report.
North Korea has relied heavily on counterfeit U.S. and European parts to produce missiles and drones used in the war against Ukraine, a new report has found, suggesting that sanctions are limiting Pyongyang’s ability to source original components. The U.K.-based Conflict Armament Research (CAR) project analyzed North Korean Hwasong-11-series missiles used by Russia against Ukraine […]
- NK News, 3 hours ago: North Korea rejects Seoul’s land mine probe, warns against DMZ demining efforts.
North Korea on Tuesday condemned South Korea’s final investigation into a land mine explosion near the inter-Korean border that injured three soldiers and warned that its forces would respond to any South Korean demining activity that crosses into the North’s territory. In a statement issued through the state-run Korean Central News Agency (KCNA), the DPRK […]
- Yonhap News Agency, 3 hours ago: (LEAD) N. Korea warns of 'powerful counteraction' if S. Korea intrudes 'even a millimeter' into its territory.
SEOUL, Oct. 6 (Yonhap) -- North Korea on Tuesday warned of an "immediate and pow...
- Yonhap News Agency, 5 hours ago: (LEAD) S. Korea, U.S. aligned on N. Korea policy, denuclearization of Korean Peninsula: FM Cho.
SEOUL, Oct. 6 (Yonhap) -- Foreign Minister Cho Hyun said Tuesday that South Kore...
India - bottom line: 11 Indians Injured After Panama-Flagged Vessel Attacked In Hormuz: Centre.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: 11 Indians Injured After Panama-Flagged Vessel Attacked In Hormuz: Centre.
The vessel, MT On Peace, carried 19 crew members, including 17 Indian nationals. In total, 12 crew members -- 11 of them Indian -- sustained injuries in the strike, according to the Ministry of External Affairs.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: K-8 attack jets, military vehicles spotted at new China-Laos air base: Report.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 2 hours ago: US, China in talks for reciprocal visits to nuclear sites in bid to build trust.
The United States intends to begin reciprocal visits to nuclear facilities in China, aiming to strengthen trust between the two nations. This proactive initiative seeks to avert a possible arms race amidst escalating worries over China's expanding nuclear arsenal. Currently, officials from both sides are engaging in preliminary talks. A pivotal meeting between US and Chinese leaders is expected later this year to enhance dialogue surrounding nuclear risks and capabilities.
- NDTV - Top Stories, 5 hours ago: Death By Firing Squad: Trump Orders Execution Of US Doctor Who Killed 13 People.
Putting former US Army Major Nidal Hasan to death by the Army firing squad was approved by Trump at the recommendation of Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth, Pentagon spokesperson Sean Parnell said.

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: Angus Taylor vows biggest cut to migration in Australia’s history, slashing 650,000 temporary visas.
- The Guardian - Australia, 11 hours ago: Angus Taylor vows biggest cut to migration in Australia’s history, slashing 650,000 temporary visas.
Opposition leader says Coalition would reduce net overseas migration to 100,000 for two years Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast Angus Taylor says a Coalition government would reduce net overseas migration to 100,000 for two years, calling the plan “the biggest cut to immigration in the history” of Australia. Following moves by One Nation and Labor to capitalise on growing anti-migration sentiment, the opposition leader announced plans by the Liberals and Nationals on Tuesday, promising net overseas migration rates of 130,000 in the third year and 160,000 in the fourth.
- ABC News Australia, 9 hours ago: Cross River Rail worker tells inquiry he 'saw red' in brawl with CFMEU members.
A commission of inquiry into the Queensland branch of the CFMEU has heard a group of workers were attacked by union members at a Cross River Rail site in Dutton Park.
- The Guardian - Australia, just now: Coalition’s migration plan risks breaching India free trade agreement and damaging economy, advocates warn.
Angus Taylor’s drastic cuts to graduate visas aim to end a citizenship pathway, but universities body says changes will make Australia less competitive Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast The Coalition’s migration plan risks breaching Australia’s free trade agreement with India, signed by the former Morrison government, allowing Indian students to stay and work for up to four years after completing their studies.
- ABC News Australia, one hour ago: Asos app users sent 'hacked' message from online retailer.
"Engage with us, or we will leak it," Asos shoppers warned in an alarming message sent from online retailer's app.

This briefing is compiled automatically from regional news feeds and has not been cross-referenced by an editor. Treat single-source claims as unconfirmed. I will be back with the next update.
